segments.label: Harper v. Virginia Board of Elections, syllabus ¶ 1
segments.text: Appellants, Virginia residents, brought this action to have Virginia's poll tax declared unconstitutional. The three-judge District Court dismissed the complaint on the basis of Breedlove v. Suttles, 302 U. S. 277. Held: A State's conditioning of the right to vote on the payment of a fee or tax violates the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment. Breedlove v. Suttles, supra, pro tanto overruled. Pp. 665-670.

segments.label: Harper v. Virginia Board of Elections, syllabus ¶ 2
segments.text: (a) Once the franchise is granted to the electorate, lines which determine who may vote may not be drawn so as to cause invidious discrimination. Pp. 665-667.

segments.label: Harper v. Virginia Board of Elections, syllabus ¶ 3
segments.text: (b) Fee l)ayments or wealth, like race, creed, or color, are unrelated to the citizen's ability to participate intelligently in the electoral process. Pp. 666-668.

segments.label: Harper v. Virginia Board of Elections, syllabus ¶ 4
segments.text: (c) The interest of the State, when it comes to voting registration, is limited to the fixing of standards related to the applicant's qualifications as a voter. P. 668.

segments.label: Harper v. Virginia Board of Elections, syllabus ¶ 5
segments.text: (d) Lines drawn on the basis of wealth or property, like those of race, are traditionall'y disfavored. P. 668.

segments.label: Harper v. Virginia Board of Elections, syllabus ¶ 6
segments.text: (e) Classifications which might impinge on fundamental rights and liberties-such as the franchise-must be closely scrutinized. P. 670.
